questiontext.text:
Two sources emit waves in phase. They are 10 cm apart and their wavelength is 4.0 cm — a setup you can build in the Two-source interference sim.

How many interference maxima does the full pattern contain (both sides, plus the one straight ahead)? (Enter a whole number.)

generalfeedback.text:
5.

Maxima occur where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, Δr = mλ. But Δr can never exceed the source separation d — that is the most extra distance one path can have. So m is limited to |m| ≤ d/λ = 10/4.0 = 2.5, giving m = 0, ±1, ±2 — five maxima in all.

This is why a real two-source pattern is not an endless row of evenly spaced fringes: the number of orders is capped by d/λ, and the ones near the edge (large angle) are spread much wider than the ones near the centre.

feedback.text: That is the highest order, m = 2 (since d/λ = 2.5). The question asks how many maxima there are — don't forget m = 0 and the matching −1, −2 on the other side.
You counted m = 0, 1, 2 — one side of the pattern. It is symmetric about the centre line, so there is an m = −1 and m = −2 as well.
Close — but d/λ = 2.5 is not itself an allowed order. m must be a whole number, so the largest is m = 2, and there is still the central m = 0.
Maxima are at Δr = mλ, and Δr cannot exceed the source separation d. Find the largest whole-number m with mλ ≤ d, then count m = 0 and both signs.

name.text: KO5-B · Constructive or destructive at a point

questiontext.text:
Two sources emit waves in phase. A point Q is 6.0 m from one source and 7.0 m from the other. The wavelength is 0.40 m.

Is Q a point of constructive or destructive interference?

generalfeedback.text:
Destructive — the waves cancel at Q.

The path difference is Δr = 7.0 m − 6.0 m = 1.0 m. In wavelengths that is 1.0 m ÷ 0.40 m = 2.5 — a half-integer. Written as (m + ½)λ with m = 2, so the second wave arrives exactly half a cycle behind: crest meets trough and they cancel.

Only the leftover fraction of a wavelength matters: 0.5λ, 1.5λ and 2.5λ all give complete cancellation; whole numbers of wavelengths give a maximum.

incorrectfeedback.text: Find the path difference, divide by the wavelength, and look at the leftover fraction: a whole number is a maximum, a half is a cancellation.

answer.text: Destructive — the two waves arrive exactly out of step and cancel

feedback.text: Correct — the path difference is 2.5 wavelengths, a half-integer.

answer.text: Constructive — the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths

feedback.text: Work out the path difference in metres, then divide by 0.40 m. Is the result a whole number, or does it land halfway between two whole numbers?

answer.text: Neither — it falls halfway between a maximum and a complete cancellation

feedback.text: A path difference of exactly 2.5 wavelengths is not an in-between case: it is one of the two extremes. Which one happens when the waves are a half-cycle apart?

answer.text: Cannot tell without knowing the distance from Q to the sources' midline

feedback.text: Constructive vs destructive at a point depends only on the two path lengths to it and the wavelength — and you already have all three numbers.
